definitions.gloss: side mirror; wing mirror; door-mounted mirror
definitions.explanation: The exterior mirror mounted on a car door for checking the rear and side views while driving. A wasei-eigo term (door + mirror) that is standard in Japanese automotive vocabulary.

examples.japanese: ドアミラー⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{調整|ちょうせい}して→調整する：10442_chouseisuru⟧⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧。
⟦{車線変更|しゃせんへんこう}→車線変更：17361_shasenhenkou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{前|まえ}→前：02255_mae⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ドアミラー⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{確認|かくにん}する→確認する：25332_kakuninsuru⟧。
examples.english: Check the side mirror before changing lanes.

examples.japanese: ⟦{狭|せま}い→狭い：00750_semai⟧⟦{道|みち}→道：00505_michi⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧ドアミラー⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{擦|こす}って→擦る：04262_kosuru⟧しまい、⟦{修理|しゅうり}→修理：03214_shuuri⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{出|だ}した→出す：01087_dasu⟧。
examples.english: I scraped the side mirror on a narrow road and had to get it repaired.

notes:
A wasei-eigo compound (English "door" + "mirror"). In English, the same part is called a "side mirror," "wing mirror" (British), or "side-view mirror." The Japanese term emphasizes the mounting location (on the door) rather than the function.

Older Japanese cars used フェンダー⟦ミラー→ミラー：25746_miraa⟧ (fender mirrors) mounted on the front fenders. Japan was one of the last countries to allow ドアミラー, which became legal in 1983 and quickly became standard. Fender mirrors are now rare but still seen on some taxis.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ドアミラー⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{調整|ちょうせい}する→調整する：10442_chouseisuru⟧: to adjust the side mirror
- ドアミラー⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{確認|かくにん}する→確認する：25332_kakuninsuru⟧: to check the side mirror
- ドアミラー⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{畳|たた}む→畳む：02073_tatamu⟧: to fold in the side mirror
- ⟦{電動|でんどう}→電動：06412_dendou⟧ドアミラー: power-folding side mirror
